title: Your Small Savings Scheme Interest Rates for October-December 2026 are Out!
description: The government has kept interest rates for most small savings schemes unchanged for October-December 2026. This is the tenth consecutive quarter with stable r.

faq.q: How often are these rates revised?
faq.a: The interest rates for small savings schemes are reviewed and revised by the Ministry of Finance on a quarterly basis.

faq.q: Can I open these accounts online?
faq.a: While some banks offer online facilities for certain small savings schemes, most are traditionally opened and operated through post offices. It's best to check with your nearest post office or specific bank for their current procedures.

faq.q: Is the interest earned from these schemes taxable?
faq.a: The taxability varies by scheme. For example, PPF offers an "Exempt-Exempt-Exempt" (EEE) status, meaning contributions, interest, and maturity amounts are tax-free. NSC interest is compounded annually but paid at maturity, and the interest is taxable, though the investment qualifies for Section 80C deduction. SCSS interest is taxable if it exceeds a certain limit. Always check the specific tax rules for each scheme.

faq.q: What is the minimum investment required for these schemes?
faq.a: The minimum investment varies by scheme. For instance, PPF requires a minimum of ₹500 per financial year, while NSC and KVP can be opened with ₹1,000.
